name: Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD)
summary: Chronic symptoms or mucosal damage from reflux of stomach contents into the esophagus. Diagnosis is clinical in many uncomplicated cases; alarm features warrant investigation.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for alarm features, symptoms not responding to short OTC courses, or age/risk factors prompting endoscopy per guidelines. Emergency care for severe chest pain that could be cardiac.
evidence_overview: Lifestyle measures and acid suppression (H2RA/PPI) are guideline-supported for typical GERD. Long-term PPI should match a clear indication.

symptoms.supporting: Worse after meals or lying down
symptoms.against: Exertional pain relieved by rest may suggest cardiac cause

symptoms.supporting: May overlap with peptic ulcer disease
symptoms.against: Severe sudden abdominal pain needs urgent evaluation

name: Peptic ulcer disease
summary: Defects in gastric or duodenal mucosa, often related to H. pylori or NSAIDs. Can present with epigastric pain; complications include bleeding and perforation.
when_to_seek_care: Urgent care for signs of bleeding or perforation. Elective evaluation for persistent epigastric pain, especially with NSAID use or prior ulcers.
evidence_overview: Test-and-treat or endoscopy strategies depend on age and alarm features. PPI and H. pylori eradication are evidence-based when indicated.

symptoms.supporting: Suggests possible upper GI bleeding — urgent care

name: Hypertension
summary: Persistently elevated blood pressure increasing long-term risk of stroke, heart disease, and kidney disease. Usually asymptomatic until complications develop.
when_to_seek_care: Confirm elevated readings with proper technique. Seek urgent care for symptoms of hypertensive emergency. Routine care for sustained elevated BP.
evidence_overview: Lifestyle and medication strategies are strongly guideline-supported (ACC/AHA, NICE, ESC).

symptoms.against: Most headaches are not caused by hypertension

name: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
summary: Disorder of insulin resistance and progressive insulin deficiency leading to hyperglycemia and microvascular/macrovascular complications.
when_to_seek_care: Urgent care for signs of DKA/HHS. Routine screening and care for risk factors or abnormal labs.
evidence_overview: ADA/EASD/NICE guidelines support metformin first-line for many, with SGLT2i/GLP-1RA for cardiorenal risk.

name: Asthma
summary: Chronic inflammatory airway disease with variable airflow obstruction and hyperresponsiveness. Symptoms often episodic and reversible.
when_to_seek_care: Emergency care for severe breathlessness or poor response to reliever. Clinical diagnosis and controller therapy planning with a clinician.
evidence_overview: GINA guidelines emphasize anti-inflammatory controller therapy; SABA-only treatment is discouraged for most adults.

name: COPD
summary: Progressive airflow limitation usually related to smoking or other exposures. Not fully reversible. Clinical assessment is required; this educational summary is not a diagnosis.
when_to_seek_care: Urgent care for exacerbations with severe breathlessness. Spirometry-confirmed diagnosis and smoking cessation support.
evidence_overview: GOLD guidelines: bronchodilators, inhaled therapies, vaccination, pulmonary rehab, smoking cessation.

name: Major depressive disorder
summary: Common mood disorder with persistent low mood and/or anhedonia plus associated cognitive and somatic symptoms lasting ≥2 weeks (diagnostic criteria require clinical assessment).
when_to_seek_care: Seek urgent/emergency help for suicidal thoughts or inability to stay safe. Professional assessment for persistent mood symptoms.
evidence_overview: NICE and other guidelines support psychotherapy and/or antidepressants based on severity; SSRIs commonly first-line pharmacotherapy in adults.

name: Generalized anxiety disorder
summary: Excessive, difficult-to-control worry about multiple domains with associated physical symptoms, causing impairment. Clinical assessment is required; this educational summary is not a diagnosis.
red_flags: panic with chest pain needing ACS exclusion
when_to_seek_care: Professional assessment for persistent anxiety impairing function. Emergency care if chest pain or safety concerns.
evidence_overview: CBT and SSRIs/SNRIs have supporting evidence; benzodiazepines for short-term selected use only.

name: Migraine
summary: Recurrent primary headache disorder, often unilateral and throbbing, with sensitivity to light/sound and/or nausea; aura may occur.
when_to_seek_care: Emergency care for thunderclap or neurologic deficits. Clinical diagnosis and preventive therapy discussion for frequent attacks.
evidence_overview: Triptans and NSAIDs for acute treatment in appropriate patients; preventive options per guidelines.

name: Urinary tract infection (cystitis)
summary: Common bacterial infection of the bladder, more frequent in women. Dysuria and frequency are typical; upper tract involvement is more serious.
when_to_seek_care: Prompt care if pregnant, male, recurrent, or systemic symptoms (possible pyelonephritis). Uncomplicated cystitis pathways vary by region.
evidence_overview: Empiric antibiotics based on local resistance; stewardship important. Fluoroquinolones reserved.

name: Community-acquired pneumonia
summary: Acute infection of the lung parenchyma acquired outside hospital. Severity ranges from mild ambulatory disease to life-threatening.
when_to_seek_care: Urgent evaluation for breathing difficulty, confusion, or high-risk patients. Do not rely on online tools for severity triage alone.
evidence_overview: Guidelines guide empiric antibiotics by setting and severity; vaccination prevention important.

name: Atrial fibrillation
summary: Common arrhythmia with irregular atrial activation, increasing stroke risk and possibly reducing cardiac efficiency. Clinical assessment is required; this educational summary is not a diagnosis.
when_to_seek_care: Urgent care for instability. Evaluation for rate/rhythm control and anticoagulation based on stroke risk scores.
evidence_overview: Strong evidence for anticoagulation in elevated stroke risk; rate vs rhythm strategies individualized.

name: Heart failure
summary: Clinical syndrome from structural/functional cardiac impairment leading to congestion and/or inadequate perfusion. Clinical assessment is required; this educational summary is not a diagnosis.
when_to_seek_care: Emergency care for acute pulmonary edema. Specialist management for confirmed HF; do not stop HF meds abruptly without advice.
evidence_overview: ESC/AHA guidelines: foundational therapy for HFrEF (ARNi/ACEI/ARB, beta-blocker, MRA, SGLT2i).

name: Hypothyroidism
summary: Thyroid hormone deficiency, most often autoimmune (Hashimoto) in iodine-sufficient regions. Treated with levothyroxine replacement.
red_flags: myxedema coma features (hypothermia, altered mental status)
when_to_seek_care: Lab confirmation (TSH/free T4). Urgent care for severe presentations. Do not adjust doses without clinician guidance.
evidence_overview: Levothyroxine is standard; monitor TSH; pregnancy needs closer follow-up.

name: Osteoarthritis
summary: Degenerative joint disease causing pain and functional limitation, commonly knees, hips, hands. Clinical assessment is required; this educational summary is not a diagnosis.
red_flags: hot swollen joint with fever (septic arthritis concern)
when_to_seek_care: Urgent care for hot swollen joint. Routine care for chronic joint pain limiting function.
evidence_overview: Exercise, weight management, topical/oral NSAIDs as appropriate; surgery for selected advanced cases.

name: Gout
summary: Crystal arthropathy from monosodium urate deposition, classically acute monoarthritis of the first MTP joint. Clinical assessment is required; this educational summary is not a diagnosis.
red_flags: fever with hot joint (must exclude infection)
when_to_seek_care: Urgent evaluation to exclude septic arthritis when uncertain. Urate-lowering therapy decisions are individualized.
evidence_overview: Anti-inflammatories for acute flares; allopurinol/febuxostat for chronic management when indicated.

synonyms: can't tolerate bed sheet on joint

name: Allergic rhinitis
summary: IgE-mediated inflammation of the nasal mucosa triggered by allergens, causing sneezing, rhinorrhea, and congestion. Clinical assessment is required; this educational summary is not a diagnosis.
red_flags: unilateral symptoms with bleeding (consider other diagnoses)
when_to_seek_care: Care for uncontrolled symptoms, asthma overlap, or uncertain diagnosis. Emergency care for anaphylaxis.
evidence_overview: Antihistamines and intranasal corticosteroids are mainstays; allergen immunotherapy selected cases.

name: Iron deficiency anemia
summary: Anemia due to insufficient iron for hemoglobin synthesis; causes include blood loss and inadequate intake/absorption. Clinical assessment is required; this educational summary is not a diagnosis.
when_to_seek_care: Lab confirmation and investigation of underlying cause (especially GI blood loss in men and postmenopausal women).
evidence_overview: Oral or IV iron as appropriate; investigate source of loss.

name: Insomnia disorder
summary: Persistent difficulty initiating or maintaining sleep with daytime impairment, despite adequate opportunity to sleep. Clinical assessment is required; this educational summary is not a diagnosis.
red_flags: restless legs with urge to move
when_to_seek_care: Evaluate for contributing conditions. CBT-I preferred long-term; hypnotics short-term selected cases.
evidence_overview: CBT-I has strongest long-term evidence; medications have dependency and safety tradeoffs.

name: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
summary: Noncancerous prostate enlargement causing lower urinary tract symptoms in aging men. Clinical assessment is required; this educational summary is not a diagnosis.
when_to_seek_care: Urgent care for acute retention. Urologic evaluation for progressive LUTS or red flags.
evidence_overview: Alpha-blockers and 5-ARIs as indicated; surgery for refractory cases.

name: Osteoporosis
summary: Low bone mass and microarchitectural deterioration increasing fracture risk; often silent until fracture. Clinical assessment is required; this educational summary is not a diagnosis.
red_flags: acute back pain after minimal trauma (vertebral fracture)
when_to_seek_care: DXA screening per age/risk guidelines. Treat after fragility fracture assessment.
evidence_overview: Bisphosphonates and other agents reduce fracture risk; calcium/vitamin D as adjunct when appropriate.

name: Acute bronchitis (typically viral)
summary: Self-limited lower airway inflammation, usually viral, with cough lasting up to 2–3 weeks. Antibiotics generally not indicated in otherwise healthy adults.
when_to_seek_care: Care if symptoms suggest pneumonia or high-risk host. Avoid unnecessary antibiotics for typical viral bronchitis.
evidence_overview: Guidelines discourage routine antibiotics for uncomplicated acute bronchitis.

symptoms.against: Color alone does not confirm bacterial infection needing antibiotics

name: COVID-19
summary: Illness caused by SARS-CoV-2 with variable severity from asymptomatic to critical respiratory failure. Management evolves with variants and immunity.
when_to_seek_care: Emergency care for breathing difficulty. Early antivirals (e.g., nirmatrelvir/ritonavir) for eligible high-risk outpatients per current guidance — interaction check essential.
evidence_overview: Vaccination reduces severe outcomes. Antivirals for high-risk early disease have RCT support; interaction screening mandatory for Paxlovid.

name: Deep vein thrombosis
summary: Blood clot in a deep vein, usually leg, that can embolize to the lungs (PE). Risk factors include immobility, surgery, cancer, hormones, prior VTE.
red_flags: massive swelling with arterial compromise signs
when_to_seek_care: Urgent medical evaluation for suspected DVT/PE — do not wait for online confirmation.
evidence_overview: Wells score + D-dimer/ultrasound pathways; anticoagulation when confirmed unless contraindicated.

name: Stroke / TIA (cerebrovascular)
summary: Acute focal neurologic deficit from ischemia or hemorrhage (stroke) or transient ischemia (TIA). Time-critical emergency.
red_flags: ANY sudden focal neurologic symptom — treat as emergency
when_to_seek_care: Call emergency services immediately (FAST). Do not drive yourself. This is not a wait-and-see situation.
evidence_overview: Thrombolysis/thrombectomy windows are time-critical. Secondary prevention includes antiplatelets/anticoagulation as indicated, BP/lipid/diabetes control.

name: Anaphylaxis
summary: Severe, life-threatening systemic hypersensitivity reaction, often rapid onset, involving airway, breathing, and/or circulation, commonly with skin changes.
when_to_seek_care: Use epinephrine if available/prescribed and call emergency services immediately. Lie flat with legs elevated if breathing allows (sit up if breathing easier).
evidence_overview: Intramuscular epinephrine is first-line. Observation for biphasic reactions; allergist follow-up and action plan.

name: Constipation (functional)
summary: Infrequent or difficult passage of stool; functional constipation is common and often lifestyle-related, but red flags need exclusion of serious causes.
red_flags: family history of CRC with concerning features
when_to_seek_care: Evaluate red flags. Trial of lifestyle and OTC measures for uncomplicated cases per local guidance.
evidence_overview: Fiber, fluids, osmotic laxatives commonly used; investigate alarm features.

name: Irritable bowel syndrome
summary: Disorder of gut-brain interaction with recurrent abdominal pain related to defecation and/or change in stool frequency/form. Diagnosis of pattern after excluding red flags.
when_to_seek_care: Clinical assessment to exclude organic disease when indicated. Not an emergency unless red flags.
evidence_overview: Positive diagnosis using symptom criteria; diet, psychological, and pharmacologic options individualized.

name: Hyperlipidemia / dyslipidemia
summary: Abnormal blood lipids increasing atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk. Usually asymptomatic until vascular events.
red_flags: very high triglycerides with pancreatitis symptoms
premature CHD family history needing cascade screening
when_to_seek_care: Cardiovascular risk assessment and lipid panel interpretation with a clinician.
evidence_overview: Statins have robust outcome evidence for risk reduction in indicated patients.

name: Chronic kidney disease
summary: Persistent reduction in kidney function or markers of kidney damage for >3 months, with staged risk based on GFR and albuminuria.
when_to_seek_care: Nephrology referral per GFR/albuminuria thresholds. Medication review for nephrotoxins and dose adjustments.
evidence_overview: ACEI/ARB, SGLT2i, BP/diabetes control slow progression in indicated populations.

name: Eczema / atopic dermatitis
summary: Chronic relapsing inflammatory skin condition with barrier dysfunction and itch. Diagnosis is clinical; secondary infection and steroid misuse are common pitfalls.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for uncontrolled itch, suspected infection, or infant involvement. Emergency care for systemic toxicity or severe widespread disease.
evidence_overview: Emollients are foundational. Topical corticosteroids/calcineurin inhibitors have trial support. Systemic agents reserved for refractory disease.

symptoms.against: Painful rapidly progressive rash needs infection/urgent eval

name: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (adult overview)
summary: Neurodevelopmental condition with persistent inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity impairing function. Adult diagnosis requires careful history; symptoms are not specific.
when_to_seek_care: Seek evaluation via qualified clinician. Emergency care for suicidal ideation or acute psychiatric crisis. This overview does not diagnose ADHD.
evidence_overview: Stimulants and atomoxetine have RCT support in diagnosed ADHD. Diagnosis must exclude mimics; online checklists are insufficient.

name: Bipolar disorder (overview)
summary: Mood disorder with episodes of mania/hypomania and often depression. Self-labeling is unreliable; stimulant/substance effects and medical causes must be considered.
red_flags: severe mania with no sleep for days
when_to_seek_care: Urgent/emergency psychiatric care for mania with risk, psychosis, or suicidality. Do not stop mood stabilizers abruptly without clinical advice.
evidence_overview: Lithium, valproate, atypical antipsychotics, and lamotrigine have role-specific evidence. Valproate is highly restricted in people who can become pregnant.

symptoms.supporting: High energy despite little sleep is concerning for mania

name: Epilepsy / seizure disorder (overview)
summary: Tendency toward unprovoked seizures. First seizure workups differ from established epilepsy management. Driving and safety counseling are essential.
when_to_seek_care: Call emergency services for prolonged/recurrent seizures (status protocols). New first seizure needs prompt medical evaluation. Never stop antiseizure meds abruptly.
evidence_overview: Multiple antiseizure medications have RCT support; choice is syndrome- and patient-specific (pregnancy, interactions, comorbidities).

name: Community-acquired pneumonia (overview)
summary: Acute infection of the lung parenchyma acquired outside hospital. Severity tools and chest imaging guide site-of-care decisions.
when_to_seek_care: Urgent care for breathing difficulty, confusion, or high-risk hosts. Emergency care for severe sepsis signs. Antibiotics are not always indicated before assessment.
evidence_overview: Empiric antibiotics follow local resistance and guidelines (e.g., IDSA/ATS, NICE). Viral pneumonia is common; stewardship matters.

symptoms.supporting: New hypoxia is a red flag
symptoms.against: Chronic stable DOE may be COPD/HF

name: Acute sinusitis (rhinosinusitis)
summary: Inflammation of paranasal sinuses, usually viral. Bacterial infection is less common; antibiotics help only selected patients.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for symptoms >10 days without improvement, severe onset, or double-worsening. Emergency care for orbital/CNS complications.
evidence_overview: Guidelines emphasize symptomatic care; antibiotics reserved for specific criteria. Imaging not routine for uncomplicated acute cases.

name: Pharyngitis / tonsillitis
summary: Sore throat from viral or bacterial (including GAS) causes. Centor/FeverPAIN-type criteria and testing reduce unnecessary antibiotics.
when_to_seek_care: Emergency care for airway concern/peritonsillar abscess signs. Testing/treatment decisions for strep should be clinician-guided.
evidence_overview: Most pharyngitis is viral. Antibiotics for confirmed/highly likely GAS reduce complications in selected settings; symptom relief is central.

name: Cellulitis
summary: Bacterial infection of skin and subcutaneous tissue. Distinguish from stasis dermatitis, DVT, and necrotizing infections.
red_flags: rapid progression with severe pain out of proportion
when_to_seek_care: Urgent evaluation for expanding erythema with systemic symptoms. Emergency care for suspected necrotizing infection.
evidence_overview: Empiric antibiotics target streptococci/MSSA; MRSA coverage when risk factors. Elevation and comorbidity management matter.

name: Deep vein thrombosis (symptom overview)
summary: Thrombosis in deep veins, usually legs. Clinical prediction rules plus D-dimer/ultrasound pathways guide diagnosis — not self-diagnosis.
red_flags: signs of PE (pleuritic pain, dyspnea, hemoptysis, syncope)
when_to_seek_care: Urgent medical assessment for possible DVT. Emergency care for PE symptoms or threatened limb. Do not start anticoagulants without clinical pathway.
evidence_overview: Anticoagulation is evidence-based once DVT/PE confirmed (or highly probable in selected protocols). Duration depends on provoked vs unprovoked and bleeding risk.

symptoms.against: Bilateral chronic edema more often venous insufficiency/HF

name: Pulmonary embolism (overview)
summary: Venous thrombus embolizing to pulmonary arteries. Presentation ranges from subtle dyspnea to collapse. Clinical assessment is required; this educational summary is not a diagnosis.
when_to_seek_care: Emergency care for suspected PE with instability. Urgent pathways for suspected PE without shock. This tool does not rule out PE.
evidence_overview: Diagnosis uses validated pathways (Wells/Geneva, D-dimer, CTPA/V/Q). Anticoagulation is standard when confirmed; thrombolysis reserved for selected massive PE.

name: Anemia (general overview)
summary: Low hemoglobin with diverse causes (iron deficiency, B12/folate, chronic disease, hemolysis, marrow disorders). Treat the cause, not only the number.
red_flags: neurologic symptoms of B12 deficiency severe
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for progressive fatigue with pallor or bleeding signs. Emergency care for unstable bleeding or cardiac ischemia symptoms.
evidence_overview: Iron therapy helps iron deficiency; other anemias need different treatments. Blind iron use can harm hemochromatosis/other states.

name: Hypoglycemia
summary: Low blood glucose causing autonomic and neuroglycopenic symptoms — commonly medication-related in diabetes. Clinical assessment is required; this educational summary is not a diagnosis.
when_to_seek_care: Treat known hypoglycemia per diabetes sick-day rules and seek help if severe/recurrent. Emergency care for seizure/unconsciousness (glucagon/EMS).
evidence_overview: Prevention focuses on medication review (insulin/sulfonylureas), meal timing, and education. Recheck glucose after treatment.

symptoms.supporting: In a person on insulin/sulfonylurea highly suggestive

name: Hyperthyroidism / thyrotoxicosis overview
summary: Excess thyroid hormone from Graves’, nodules, thyroiditis, or excess replacement. Symptoms overlap anxiety. Clinical assessment is required; this educational summary is not a diagnosis.
when_to_seek_care: Prompt clinician evaluation for suspected thyrotoxicosis. Emergency care for storm features. Do not adjust levothyroxine independently without advice.
evidence_overview: Antithyroid drugs, beta blockers for symptoms, radioiodine, and surgery are pathway-dependent. TSH suppression on replacement needs dose review.

name: Parkinson disease (overview)
summary: Neurodegenerative movement disorder with bradykinesia plus rest tremor/rigidity. Mimics include drug-induced parkinsonism.
red_flags: sudden high fever with rigidity on antipsychotics (NMS)
when_to_seek_care: Neurology evaluation for suspected Parkinsonism. Emergency care for NMS-like presentations or serious aspiration.
evidence_overview: Levodopa remains most effective motor therapy; timing, complications, and non-motor symptoms need specialist frameworks.

name: Rheumatoid arthritis (overview)
summary: Autoimmune inflammatory arthritis, typically symmetric small joints, with systemic features and erosive potential. Clinical assessment is required; this educational summary is not a diagnosis.
red_flags: hot swollen joint with fever (septic arthritis concern)
when_to_seek_care: Rheumatology referral for suspected RA. Emergency care for septic arthritis possibility (single hot joint + fever).
evidence_overview: Early DMARD therapy (methotrexate anchor) improves outcomes. Steroids bridge; biologics/tsDMARDs for inadequate response.

name: Psoriasis
summary: Immune-mediated skin disease with plaques; associated with psoriatic arthritis and cardiometabolic comorbidity. Clinical assessment is required; this educational summary is not a diagnosis.
when_to_seek_care: Dermatology care for moderate-severe disease. Urgent care for unstable widespread pustular/erythrodermic psoriasis.
evidence_overview: Topicals for limited disease; phototherapy/systemics/biologics for more extensive disease per guidelines.

name: Menopause / vasomotor symptoms
summary: Permanent cessation of menses with estrogen decline; vasomotor symptoms and genitourinary syndrome are common. Clinical assessment is required; this educational summary is not a diagnosis.
red_flags: chest pain with hot sensations that could be cardiac
when_to_seek_care: Discuss symptoms with clinician; postmenopausal bleeding needs evaluation. Emergency care for possible cardiac chest pain.
evidence_overview: Menopausal hormone therapy is most effective for vasomotor symptoms when appropriate; non-hormonal options exist. Risk–benefit is individualized (age, time since menopause, VTE/breast cancer risks).

name: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (LUTS)
summary: Prostate enlargement contributing to lower urinary tract symptoms in many aging men. Overlap with infection, cancer, and neurologic bladder.
when_to_seek_care: Urgent care for acute urinary retention. Evaluate infection/hematuria red flags. Discuss PSA testing pros/cons with clinician.
evidence_overview: Alpha blockers and 5-ARIs have evidence for LUTS/BPH; surgery for refractory obstruction. Rule out mimics.

name: Overactive bladder
summary: Urgency with or without urge incontinence, usually with frequency/nocturia, without infection or other obvious pathology.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for hematuria, pain, or neurologic signs. Discuss behavioral therapies before/along with drugs.
evidence_overview: Bladder training and fluid management first-line. Antimuscarinics/beta-3 agonists have trial support; cognitive effects matter in elderly.

name: Glaucoma (chronic open-angle overview)
summary: Optic neuropathy often related to intraocular pressure, causing irreversible field loss if untreated. Early disease is asymptomatic.
red_flags: acute severe eye pain with nausea/halos (angle-closure)
when_to_seek_care: Emergency care for acute angle-closure symptoms. Routine eye exams detect open-angle disease early — not a symptom-first diagnosis.
evidence_overview: Pressure-lowering drops, laser, and surgery have evidence to slow progression. Adherence is critical.

name: Otitis media (acute)
summary: Middle ear infection common in children; adults less often. Distinguish from otitis externa and referred pain. Clinical assessment is required; this educational summary is not a diagnosis.
when_to_seek_care: Urgent care for severe symptoms or under-3 months with fever. Emergency for mastoiditis/neurologic signs.
evidence_overview: Many cases are viral/self-limited; antibiotics when criteria met (age, severity, bilateral). Analgesia is essential.

name: Conjunctivitis (overview)
summary: Conjunctival inflammation — viral, bacterial, or allergic. Red flags distinguish sight-threatening disease. Clinical assessment is required; this educational summary is not a diagnosis.
red_flags: contact lens with white cornea spot
when_to_seek_care: Urgent ophthalmology for pain/photophobia/vision change/contact-lens keratitis suspicion. Allergic/viral cases often supportive.
evidence_overview: Avoid steroid drops without diagnosis. Antibiotics only when bacterial likely; stewardship important.

name: Low back pain (nonspecific overview)
summary: Most acute low back pain is nonspecific and improves with time. Red flags identify fracture, infection, cauda equina, malignancy.
red_flags: history of cancer with night pain
when_to_seek_care: Emergency care for cauda equina signs. Urgent care for infection/cancer red flags. Imaging not routine early without red flags.
evidence_overview: Stay active, brief NSAID/analgesic courses if appropriate, and reassurance. Chronic pathways emphasize exercise and psychosocial factors.

name: Tension-type headache
summary: Common primary headache with pressing bilateral pain and mild-moderate intensity, lacking migraine features usually. Clinical assessment is required; this educational summary is not a diagnosis.
red_flags: new headache in pregnancy / cancer / immunosuppression
when_to_seek_care: Emergency care for thunderclap or meningism. Recurrent headaches warrant clinician diagnosis to avoid missing migraine/secondary causes.
evidence_overview: Simple analgesics carefully to avoid medication-overuse headache; non-drug approaches emphasized. Not an excuse to miss secondary headache.

name: Medication-overuse headache
summary: Chronic headache from frequent acute headache medication use (often ≥10–15 days/month depending on agent). Diagnosis requires clinician input.
when_to_seek_care: Discuss prevention strategies with clinician; abrupt withdrawal of some agents needs supervision. Emergency for red-flag headaches.
evidence_overview: Prevention with appropriate prophylaxis and structured withdrawal of overused acute meds is guideline-supported.
